title: Entitlement Recon and SIEM Export Playbook - Q3 2026
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures the approach for the Q3 entitlement recon and the SIEM export schema to support quarterly least-privilege recertification. Goal is to produce deterministic, auditable evidence bundles for each access-review cohort and ensure RBAC v2 deltas are traceable from request -> policy evaluation -> enforcement.

Scope:
- All privileged groups (org-admins, infra-admins, model-oncall, billing-admin) and service principals with write access to production clusters.
- RBAC v2 role definitions and role-bindings across Hosted API, Dedicated control plane, and Private deployments.
- Audit log fields to be exported to SIEM and included in evidence bundles for recertification.
- Automation steps to collect, validate, and store evidence for reviewers.

High-level flow:
1) Entitlement snapshot: nightly job produces current entitlements for each cohort.
2) Delta detection: compare snapshot to previous quarter baseline; flag new grants, escalations, and stale entitlements.
3) Evidence assembly: for each flagged entitlement, collect: grant event, policy-eval transcript, last-use timestamp, and if applicable, justification doc/ticket ID.
4) SIEM export: push normalized audit records (see schema) to SIEM (Splunk/Chronicle) with export tagging for recertification run id.
5) Reviewer bundle: generate a zip per reviewer containing entries in CSV + human-friendly notes and links to tickets/PRs.

Key definitions and naming conventions:
- recert_run_id: RECERT-<YYYYMM>-<cohort> (e.g., RECERT-202606-org-admins)
- evidence_bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/recert/<recert_run_id>/
- snapshot_time: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the entitlement snapshot.
- actor_identity_type: human | service-account | third-party-integration

RBAC v2 delta rules (short):
- New grant: principal appears in role-binding and not in baseline.
- Escalation: principal gains a role with strictly greater privilege set than any prior assignment.
- Lateral change: role assignment moved from one binding to another but privilege set unchanged (flag for audit only).
- Stale: no recorded usage in last 90 days -> auto-flag for deprovisioning recommendation.

SIEM export schema (recommended canonical fields):
- timestamp: ISO-8601 string (string)
- recert_run_id: string (as above)
- event_type: entitlement_snapshot | grant_event | policy_eval | access_attempt | deprovision_action
- request_id: UUID string for traceability across systems
- actor_id: principal id (email or service account)
- actor_identity_type: human | service-account | integration
- resource_type: e.g. project, model, deployment, console-route
- resource_path: canonical resource identifier (string)
- role_assigned: role name from RBAC v2 (string)
- permission_granted: comma-separated permission list (string)
- policy_decision: allow | deny | conditional
- decision_reason: short text from policy engine (string)
- last_used: ISO-8601 or null
- evidence_links: semicolon-separated URLs (ticket, PR, key-rotation doc)
- operator: person or automation agent who performed the action
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- raw_audit_blob_ref: pointer to raw log file in evidence_bucket (s3 path)
- siem_priority: low | medium | high (mapping rule below)

Mapping rules and examples:
- Grant event (IAM system): event_type=grant_event, request_id from IAM, actor_id is grantee, role_assigned set, permission_granted resolved from role catalog, policy_decision should be pre-check summary or 'n/a' if no policy runtime check.
- Policy evaluation record (OPA/External PDP): event_type=policy_eval, request_id matches request that triggered the eval, policy_decision and decision_reason populated.
- Access attempt: event_type=access_attempt, last_used updated to timestamp, outcome set based on enforcement.

SIEM priority heuristic (automated):
- high: role_assigned includes any of [org-admin, infra-admin, secrets-admin] OR service-account with write access to production + no recent owner contact info.
- medium: write privileges to non-sensitive resources or read to sensitive resources.
- low: read-only to general resources, service accounts with narrow scope.

Evidence automation playbook (step-by-step):
1) Trigger: recert job scheduled (quarterly) or manually kicked by security ops.
2) Snapshot job: run entitlement-collector -> uploads snapshot.csv to evidence_bucket with recert_run_id tag.
3) Delta engine: run entitlement-diff against baseline; generate delta.csv.
4) For each delta row spawn evidence-collector lambda:
   - query audit-log-store for grant_event and policy_eval traces (window: grant_time -1h to +24h)
   - query usage-index for last_used and request patterns
   - attach related Jira/PR links via heuristics (principal email -> recent PR authorship, ticket mentions)
   - write evidence.json (flat record) and append pointer to raw audit blob into evidence_bucket/recert_run_id/
5) Validation: schema-checker job ensures every evidence.json contains required SIEM fields; failures create JIRA-SEC issues automatically.
6) Reviewer bundle generator: aggregates evidence.json into reviewer CSVs and a short summary.md with top-risk items.
7) Delivery: email to reviewers with signed presigned links and an expiration (default 30 days).

Reviewer guidance (for the Q3 run):
- Focus first on 'high' priority items. Confirm whether the principal still requires the role by looking at: recent requests, active tickets, and product-owner approval.
- If 'stale', recommend revocation and tag for 7-day grace re-notification.
- For service-accounts, require documented owner and last-rotate <= 90 days or escalate to infra.
- Mark each reviewed row with decision: keep | revoke | escalate. Optional comments required for keep/escalate.

Open questions / risks to surface to leadership:
- Baseline trustworthiness: our baseline snapshot comes from two sources (IAM dump + infra role-binding crawler). They diverge ~0.6% — need a reconciliation job and an owner.
- Policy-eval coverage: not all enforcement points emit policy_eval traces (legacy infra). We need a roadmap to instrument those (see linked GH PR).
- Retention: evidence retention policy for recert buckets (current ask: 1 year encrypted-at-rest). Confirm legal retention requirements for EMEA.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- (Priya) Draft reconciliation job spec + acceptance tests. ETA: 2026-03-23.
- (Marcus) Add policy_eval hooks for two legacy controllers (billing-proxy, deploy-gateway). ETA: 2026-04-07.
- (Evan) Implement schema-checker and auto-JIRA for failures. ETA: 2026-03-30.
- (SRE) Add SIEM export filter to include recert_run_id tag and ensure index partitioning. ETA: 2026-03-16.

Appendix A — Example evidence bundle entry (flat CSV row)
recert_run_id,timestamp,event_type,request_id,actor_id,actor_identity_type,resource_type,resource_path,role_assigned,permission_granted,policy_decision,decision_reason,last_used,evidence_links,operator,outcome,raw_audit_blob_ref,siem_priority
RECERT-202606-org-admins,2026-06-01T03:12:22Z,grant_event,1f8e9a2a-...,jdoe@redwood.ai,human,project,projects/redwood-api,org-admin,"*:*",n/a,requested_via-jira-SEC-101,2026-05-14T11:00:00Z,https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SEC-101;https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/144,iam-service,success,s3://redwood-evidence/recert/RECERT-202606-org-admins/raw/1f8e9a2a.json,high

Appendix B — Quick audit checklist for engineers running an adhoc review:
- Is there a matching grant_event and policy_eval for the role assignment?
- Is the "last_used" timestamp within 90 days? If not, check for automation-only usages (cron) before recommending removal.
- Does the evidence include a ticket or PR that justifies the grant? If missing, flag as incomplete evidence.

Notes and conversational fragments (working area):
- Consider adding an "owner_contact" field in SIEM payload for easier reviewer follow-up.
- Could we auto-suggest revocations for stale items; mail owner once and if no response deprovision? Needs legal sign-off.
- Is 1 year retention too short for customers who require 3+ years? Ops said cost will jump.

Next steps:
- Finalize schema and sample payloads (Marcus + Evan).
- Run pilot recert for "model-oncall" cohort in April to validate end-to-end.
- Present pilot findings to GRC and Product Security by 2026-05-15.

End of playbook (working draft).
